Please review /papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/brainstorm/01_RH_IMPLIES_SIMPLICITY_20261020.md and the corresponding research-overview and research-progress files within 10_rh_implies_simple_zeros. Note that this direction came out of research in 04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/09_expanding_contour_later_collision, so please also review the manuscript there. The goal is to use the machinery there to prove the conjecture that RH implies the simple zeros hypothesis. Presumably this is a more achievable goal than proving RH directly but would still mark significant progress, so we have decided to make a parallel research track to investigate it directly.

Please begin the investigation, provide your research notes in the notes folder, and update your progress within research-progress/01_RH_TO_SIMPLICITY_PROGRESS_20261020.  Continue until all tasks are finished or you run out of compute budget. Save the chat within 10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/chat-histories.
I’ll read the research guidance, the new simplicity track, and the earlier contour manuscript, then investigate the proof routes and record the findings in the notes and progress files.

The opening files correctly identify the gap: RH rules out later collisions, but the local splitting formulas still allow a multiple zero at time zero. I’m testing whether the exact zeta coefficients add a useful restriction that the modified Euler-factor control fails, while separate checks examine the phase and Gaussian estimates.

There is a useful advance in the contour setup: under RH, the roots emerging from a hypothetical multiple zero can be followed to every finite positive time. But their total phase remains exactly the expected baseline. The arithmetic calculation also detects the control’s added double zeros explicitly; standard bounds on the prime terms are too coarse to exclude multiplicity at arbitrary height.

The next arithmetic check gives a sharper limitation. For a finite-prime formula with a squared-sinc test function, optimizing the bound obtained by taking absolute values of the prime terms still gives roughly \(\tfrac12\log\gamma/\log\log\gamma\), which grows beyond two. This identifies the cancellation that a successful estimate would need. I’m recording the derivation and having the constants and scope checked independently.

The internal reviews found no substantive mathematical error; I’ve incorporated two wording corrections to keep the claims precise. The exact algebra checks also passed. I’m saving the notes and updating the tracker to distinguish the completed finite-wall result from the still-missing signed arithmetic estimate.

Reviewed the requested material and saved two analytical rounds. **RH ⇒ simplicity remains unproved.**

The main findings are:

- Under RH, the emerging roots continue to every finite positive time, resolving the finite-wall requirement.
- Their phase remains exactly the expected baseline; positivity alone supplies no surplus.
- Exact arithmetic tests distinguish the Euler-factor control, but the tested absolute-value estimates remain too weak. The missing step is a signed arithmetic bound.

Saved the [research notes](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/notes/README.md) and updated the [progress tracker](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/research-progress/01_RH_TO_SIMPLICITY_PROGRESS_20261020.md), preserving the unresolved tasks.

Two internal reviews and 265 exact algebra checks passed. This chat is registered as **0004** in the requested folder; capture of this final reply is arranged.

The previous round made concrete progress and saved it. I’ll now test whether retaining the signed prime information can improve the multiplicity estimate, starting from the current notes and progress register.

The signed-prime calculation exposes the next gap more clearly: the ordinary RH bound for the prime-counting error is also satisfied, eventually, by the exact double-zero control. Separately, I found a quantitative way to reject every finite Euler-polynomial modification of this type using zeta’s nonnegative logarithmic coefficients. The remaining question is how to turn that coefficient information into an estimate for a single hypothetical multiple zeta zero.

The latest calculations identify a useful distinction: zeta’s nonnegative logarithmic coefficients rule out a whole finite family of the multiple-zero controls. That still leaves a precise gap—an isolated multiple zeta zero need not arise from one of those factors. I’m checking this limitation alongside the signed-prime estimate before saving the next research note.

The review confirmed the formulas and strengthened the control check: for suitable primes, the multiple-zero control satisfies the exact RH prime-error bound used in the argument, including its constants. I’m consolidating this result with the coefficient test and recording the missing step: neither estimate yet forces a contour surplus or excludes a multiple zeta zero.

The notes and progress update are drafted, with the signed-prime and coefficient calculations checked by separate agents using the same model. The missing step remains an estimate that contradicts a hypothetical multiple zeta zero. I’m making one final control check to test whether unchanged degree and conductor can help supply that step.

That final check produced a stronger control: assuming RH, a positive-source modification can retain the same gamma factor, conductor one and pole order while adding an isolated pair of double zeros. It fails the ordinary Dirichlet-series requirement. This shows why degree and conductor alone cannot fill the gap; the proof needs an estimate using more of zeta’s arithmetic.

The continuation is saved, and the file checks passed. I’m recording a local research checkpoint so the draft history can point to the reviewed version. The progress register keeps the arithmetic estimate and strict-surplus tasks open; this work does not prove RH implies simplicity.

Saved [three research notes](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/notes/README.md), internal reviews, and the [updated progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/research-progress/01_RH_TO_SIMPLICITY_PROGRESS_20261020.md).

The work establishes:

- Finite root-wall continuation under RH.
- Explicit coefficient tests rejecting the finite Euler-polynomial controls.
- Quantitative failures of the tested arithmetic estimates, including the signed-prime approach.
- A stronger control showing that the gamma factor and conductor alone cannot force simplicity.

**RH ⇒ simplicity remains unproved; no multiple theta zero has been excluded.** The missing step is a quantitative estimate using zeta’s unchanged arithmetic that contradicts a hypothetical multiple zero. The corresponding tasks remain open.

Research checkpoint: `f418968`. Chat 0004 is archived in the requested `chat-histories` folder, with final-message capture arranged.

The previous turn made concrete progress: it saved and reviewed new arithmetic bounds and controls. I’ll now check the current files and test whether subtracting the contribution of neighboring zeros can improve the multiplicity estimate.

Subtracting neighboring zeros is valid when their locations and counts are independently established. I now have explicit bounds for the remaining tail and for location errors. Higher derivatives also sharpen the test while keeping the prime series convergent, but the tested absolute-value bound grows exponentially with derivative order. These results clarify the precision needed for a useful contradiction.

The new estimates have passed independent checks within the same model. They quantify two obstacles: a fixed-width test needs roughly \((\log \gamma)^2\) certified neighboring zeros to reduce its remaining background to a constant, and sharpening the test with derivatives makes the absolute prime-sum bound grow rapidly. I’m saving the derivations with their limits stated explicitly; neither excludes a multiple zeta zero yet.

The sharper tail result also checks out: deleting every neighboring contribution within a radius proportional to \(\log \gamma\) leaves an explicit, nonzero limiting tail. The notes will distinguish this necessary cost from the sufficient error bounds used for certification, and state what location, count, and arithmetic estimates a valid subtraction would require.

The consolidated note now gives the exact asymptotic scale for the derivative-based bound and a separate check of positive trigonometric combinations of the prime sums. Both remain too large to prove simplicity. The progress register will preserve those findings while keeping the required strict arithmetic estimate marked as unresolved.

The note and review are saved, and the overview and progress register have been updated. The internal review also caught precision issues that are now fixed: integer recovery needs an interval of width below one, the central multiplicity must remain unknown during subtraction, and location uncertainty must be included in the arithmetic evaluation.

Saved [Note 04](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/notes/04_ZERO_DEFLATION_AND_RATIONAL_RESOLUTION_20261020.md), its internal review, and updated the overview and [progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/research-progress/01_RH_TO_SIMPLICITY_PROGRESS_20261020.md).

The new results quantify neighboring-zero subtraction costs and prove the optimized limitation of the tested derivative-based arithmetic bound. They clarify what additional information a successful argument needs.

**RH ⇒ simplicity remains unproved; no multiple zeta zero has been excluded.** The strict arithmetic estimate remains unresolved.

Local checkpoint: `228d59d`. Chat history was refreshed in the requested folder, with capture of this final reply arranged.

The previous turn made progress: it saved reviewed estimates for zero subtraction and derivative-based tests. I’ll check the saved state, then examine whether the exact theta source supplies a constraint that those estimates missed.

A more informative control has emerged. It appears possible to merge two neighboring high zeros into a double zero while keeping the source positive and uniformly close to the theta source, preserving its leading tail. I’m checking this construction because it would identify precisely why source approximation and large-time shape information alone cannot settle the question.

The construction now also preserves pole residue one and the stated completion normalizations. Its arithmetic failure is explicit: along the positive real axis it has an algebraic correction that an ordinary Dirichlet series cannot have. This keeps the conclusion narrow: the control tests source approximation and normalization arguments, while the exact arithmetic step remains open.

The independent checks passed. I’m saving the normalized source construction and its review, and updating the progress register to keep its conclusion precise: it rules out several approximation-based arguments, but the estimate needed to exclude multiple zeros of the actual zeta function remains open.

The new note and review are saved, and the progress and overview files now reflect them. The construction identifies an arithmetic requirement that approximation alone cannot replace. Mathematical cross-checks and file checks passed; I’m recording the research checkpoint and refreshing the chat archive.

Saved another reviewed research checkpoint. **RH ⇒ simplicity remains unproved.**

The main new result constructs, under RH, positive sources arbitrarily close to theta that retain its leading tail, completion factors and pole residue one, yet have double zeros. Their Dirichlet-series arithmetic fails explicitly. This shows why those structural properties and fixed approximation accuracy alone cannot finish the proof.

- [Note 05: construction and scoped conclusions](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/notes/05_CLOSE_POSITIVE_SOURCES_AND_NORMALIZED_DOUBLE_ZEROS_20261020.md)
- [Internal mathematical review](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/reviews/05_SOURCE_CONTROL_AND_SHIFT_AUDIT_20261020.md)

The overview, research history and chat archive were updated. Commit: `7b3edf0`. The remaining task is an estimate using unchanged zeta arithmetic that forces the required strict surplus or opposing Gaussian sign.

The last round produced a reviewed source-control result. I’ll now return to the missing arithmetic estimate and test whether signed prime correlations provide information that the earlier absolute-value bounds lost.

Two quantitative tests are taking shape. One checks whether positivity of squared prime sums improves the earlier bound; the other measures how accurately a correlation estimate must be localized to detect one multiple zero. I’m keeping those distinct from proportion results, which can still allow isolated multiple zeros.

The correlation calculation has yielded a sharp cost: for the proposed squared-sinc statistic on a window of width \(W\) containing \(N\) zeros, certifying simplicity requires bandwidth at least \((1/2+o(1))N^{3/2}/W\). Contributions from neighboring simple zeros impose this cost before arithmetic error enters. This favors testing smaller, fully accounted windows.

The reciprocal-zeta calculation also gives a precise benchmark: a double zero would force a cubic divergence in a weighted Möbius energy, with an explicit positive constant. The checked RH upper bounds still allow that divergence. I’m consolidating these findings into one note, with the missing signed-correlation estimate stated explicitly.

The prime-phase audit is complete: universal positivity improves the old bound by one additive unit asymptotically, while leaving its divergent leading term unchanged. The cross-reviews passed after correcting one endpoint qualifier. The progress register will keep estimates using actual height or multiple-zero conditions open; this calculation does not cover them.

Saved [Note 06](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/notes/06_SIGNED_CORRELATION_RESOLUTION_AND_MOBIUS_ENERGY_20261020.md) and its internal review. Three quantitative findings:

- The tested full-window correlation certificate requires bandwidth \(\Delta W\ge(1/2+o(1))N^{3/2}\), even before arithmetic error.
- Universal prime-phase positivity saves only one additive unit over the earlier bound.
- A double zero forces an explicit cubic divergence in weighted Möbius energy; no contradictory upper bound was obtained.

**RH ⇒ simplicity remains unproved.** The [progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/research-progress/01_RH_TO_SIMPLICITY_PROGRESS_20261020.md), overview, research history and chat archive are updated. Commit: `38a8b90`.

The previous round established quantitative limits on the tested correlation methods. I’ll now examine localized estimates that use the hypothetical multiple-zero conditions, and check whether the contour machinery gains anything over direct detection of that zero.

The localized comparison gives a useful simplification: the quadratic correlation test is dominated by a matched linear zero-counting test. The Jensen-polynomial route also needs care: RH already gives strict finite approximants, even if the limiting function has a multiple zero. I’m quantifying the loss of margin in that limit.

At a hypothetical double zero, the Jensen approximants split it into two simple roots separated by order \(d^{-1/2}\), while their Laguerre margin falls like \(1/d\). This explains why strictness at every finite degree does not settle simplicity of the limit. I’ll record that rate and the localized correlation comparison in one note, with the proof gates left open.

The separate internal checks agree on both comparisons. Conditioning a finite zeta approximation on a double zero also leaves a specific gap: converting it to a logarithmic-derivative estimate needs a lower bound for the deflated zeta function. No such bound emerged. I’m saving the results and updating the progress register without marking an event exclusion.

The note, internal review, and progress updates are saved in commit `ee683628`. The record keeps the two quantitative comparisons separate from the still-missing signed estimate needed to exclude a multiple zero. I’m completing the chat capture in this investigation’s existing archive.

Saved [Note 07](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/notes/07_LOCAL_CORRELATION_AND_JENSEN_MARGIN_COMPARISONS_20261020.md) and its internal review.

Two results sharpen the investigation:

- Localized nonnegative quadratic certificates imply matched linear certificates at the same bandwidth.
- At a hypothetical multiplicity-\(m\) zero, finite Jensen roots separate at scale \(d^{-1/2}\), while their positive Laguerre margin decays like \(d^{1-m}\). Finite strictness therefore does not establish limiting simplicity.

**RH ⇒ simplicity remains unproved.** No original theta multiple zero has been excluded; the missing signed arithmetic estimate remains the central task.

Updated the research overview, [progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/research-progress/01_RH_TO_SIMPLICITY_PROGRESS_20261020.md), draft history, and chat archive. Research checkpoint: `ee683628`.

The previous round added two quantitative comparisons. I’ll now test what exact arithmetic information could overcome them, focusing on the missing margin at a putative multiple zero. I’ll also verify the saved checkpoint and chat capture before continuing.

A checked RH estimate gives a useful improvement: it bounds \(1/\zeta\) strongly enough just to the right of the critical line that a longer finite zeta sum can approximate the normalized logarithmic derivative with error tending to zero. That removes the specific approximation-precision obstacle from the last round, though it does not yet give the sign needed for simplicity.

Two further bounds checked out. The reciprocal-zeta estimate sharpens the recorded Möbius-energy upper bound, although it still permits the cubic divergence caused by a double zero. Separately, positivity forces large prime payments for a broad class of bandlimited kernels—even with signed Fourier coefficients—so changing the Fejér kernel within that class does not improve the leading bound.

Independent review has verified the finite-sum and energy estimates, including bounded heights where multiple zeros remain possible. The kernel result has an explicit limit: it covers \(I\Delta<2\), where \(I\) is the kernel’s integral and \(\Delta\) its bandwidth, and requires the gamma and pole terms to be fully accounted for. It is not a bound against every kernel choice.

The new estimates are ready to save. I’m checking the final notes, cross-references, and progress register, with the remaining gap stated explicitly: these results improve precision and bound certain approaches, but do not yet exclude a multiple zero.

The final checks passed, and I corrected two equation-reference formatting errors. Note 08 records a controlled finite-sum approximation, a stronger reciprocal-energy bound, and a lower cost bound for a specified kernel class. The progress register still marks the signed estimate and strict winding surplus as unresolved.

The checkpoint is saved in commit `989504e`, with its history entry in `31f4d65`. The notes, review, overview, and progress register are updated; all 96 local references and file-size checks passed. I’m finishing the chat capture in the requested folder.

Saved [Note 08](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/notes/08_RECIPROCAL_PRECISION_AND_BANDLIMITED_ARITHMETIC_COSTS_20261020.md), establishing:

- Controlled finite-sum approximation at distance \(c/\log\gamma\).
- A stronger reciprocal-energy upper bound.
- A sharp leading cost for a specified class of bandlimited kernels.

Separate internal review passed. The overview and [progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/research-progress/01_RH_TO_SIMPLICITY_PROGRESS_20261020.md) are updated, and the chat archive refreshed with final-reply capture arranged.

**RH ⇒ simplicity remains unproved:** the required signed estimate and strict winding surplus remain open.

Research checkpoint: `989504e`; history entry: `31f4d65`.

The previous turn made concrete progress by saving the reviewed estimates. I’ll now test whether the finite-sum precision can support a signed estimate, and examine the kernel classes left outside Note 08. I’ll first verify the checkpoint and chat capture.

Two constructions are emerging that help identify the missing input. One preserves nonnegative Dirichlet coefficients and any prescribed finite coefficient block while inserting a multiple zero, but loses the exact functional equation. The other can cancel many absolute prime contributions by adding a distant kernel peak; its displacement must still be paid for in the full height estimate.

A more direct quantitative gain has also checked out: with an independently certified gap around a zero, several logarithmic-derivative evaluations can recover its multiplicity with much less leakage from neighboring zeros. The error amplification stays below two. This improves the stated extraction method, but still returns two at a double zero—it does not force simplicity.

The internal reviews passed all three results. The kernel construction shows that the fixed margin below \(I\Delta=2\) in Note 08 is essential: three translated peaks can make the absolute prime contribution tend to zero, though no improved full height bound follows. I’m saving that distinction alongside the normalized arithmetic control and the extraction-cost improvement.

The final check caught and corrected a cross-reference and an overly broad sentence. The result refutes an unrestricted extension of Note 08’s particular prime-cost bound; it does not rule out every possible bound. The notes now state that scope consistently.

Saved the research in commit `d456990`, with history entry `47624c9`. The overview and progress register are updated, and all 101 local references and file-size checks passed. The remaining proof task is still a signed estimate for the unchanged zeta function that excludes a multiple zero.

The previous turn made concrete progress. I’ll now examine the unresolved height cost of the translated kernels: their small prime contribution is useful only if the simultaneous phase return occurs soon enough. In parallel, I’ll continue testing the exact finite-sum route for a signed estimate. First I’ll verify the saved checkpoint and chat capture.

The return-height argument has checked out against a primary source. Under RH, the simultaneous prime alignment used in Note 09 must occur at a very large height. After paying that height cost, the two-copy and three-copy constructions have leading costs at least \(1\) and \(3/2\), respectively, versus \(1/2\) for the earlier Fejér choice. This closes that particular construction as an improvement; it does not rule out other kernels.
I’m checking the proof and its scope before saving the checkpoint. The result resolves the height cost of the specific prime-alignment construction; the broader RH-to-simplicity problem remains open.

The internal checks agree on the bound. RH forces the two-copy and three-copy constructions to pay enough in height that neither improves the earlier Fejér estimate. I’m recording that scoped conclusion and updating the progress register.

The final review caught a scope distinction: only the translated sum approaches the mass–bandwidth threshold from below; the scalar-square version approaches it without that guarantee. I’m correcting that wording. The return-height bound and full-cost comparison hold for both.

Saved [Note 10](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/notes/10_UNIFORM_PRIME_PHASE_RETURN_HEIGHT_COST_20261020.md), its internal review, and updated overview/progress files.

Under RH, the specific prime-alignment constructions require such large heights that their complete costs exceed the earlier Fejér estimate. This closes that proposed improvement while preserving the small prime-payment examples.

**RH ⇒ simplicity remains unproved.** The signed arithmetic estimate remains the next gate.

Checkpoint: `69da356`. Chat history refreshed; final-response capture queued.

The previous turn made progress by resolving one return-height cost. I’ll now test whether the same RH input constrains broader translated kernels, and separately look for a signed estimate that could advance the simplicity argument.

A broader bound is taking shape. Retaining every prime power and averaging Poisson’s identity appears to extend the leading cost limit to positive mixtures of translated Fejér kernels whose translation diameter grows at most polynomially with height. I’m checking that the bound stays uniform as the number of copies and bandwidth grow.

The checks support a stronger result: the argument covers every nonnegative bandlimited kernel in the existing admissible class, provided the stated gamma and pole error bounds hold. Small prime cost requires a large logarithmic spread in the kernel, and the gamma bound limits that spread. This extends the \(1/2\) leading cost barrier beyond the earlier restricted classes; it still supplies no signed estimate that excludes a multiple zero.

The proof and integration review pass the internal checks. I’m saving the general bound and updating the older notes and progress register. The next attempt needs a justified signed arithmetic gain or a different method; changing kernels within this complete absolute-payment class cannot improve its leading cost.

Saved [Note 11](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/10_rh_implies_simple_zeros/notes/11_FULL_ABSOLUTE_PRIME_ENVELOPE_AND_LOGARITHMIC_SPREAD_20261020.md) and its internal review.

The new result extends the sharp leading \(1/2\) absolute-prime cost barrier to **every admissible nonnegative bandlimited kernel with the stated gamma and pole budgets**. Changing kernels within that class cannot overcome the barrier.

**RH ⇒ simplicity remains unproved.** A justified signed arithmetic estimate remains necessary.

Updated the overview, progress register, earlier notes and result index. Checkpoint: `6d9c19d`. Chat refreshed; final-response capture queued.

The previous turn made progress by closing the complete absolute-prime envelope comparison. I’ll now examine signed arithmetic at a putative multiple zero and test whether the heat-flow dynamics force a quantitative consequence that could contradict it.

The new checks are identifying where the estimates fail: a smoothed inverse-zeta sum still carries a large reciprocal-zeta error, and the heat-flow energy argument needs an interval of real zeros that RH alone does not supply. I’m also checking whether a sharper classical evaluation formula can reduce the cost of the existing multiplicity test.

A useful improvement has emerged in the evaluation step. A Riemann–Siegel expansion can replace the earlier long zeta sum, and a discrete Cauchy formula can estimate the derivative without differentiating its changing cutoff. I’m checking the complete error against the small zeta values allowed by RH. This would make multiplicity extraction cheaper; it would still return two at a double zero.

The sharper evaluation also changes the comparison: it gives both the geometric-width extractor and the simpler one-width test the same leading square-root summand count. Separately, the tested sign-changing kernels have nonnegative companions with smaller exact zero sums. I’m saving these scoped findings, including the error terms that still prevent a simplicity proof.

The notes and progress register are saved. The separate same-model reviews found no remaining defect in the stated calculations; one heat-energy wording issue was corrected. RH ⇒ simplicity remains unproved: the missing step is still an inequality from unchanged zeta arithmetic that conflicts with a multiple zero.
